decisions.statement: Retained legacy migration backups must be ignored by Git
decisions.reasoning: Backups may contain generated state, telemetry, credentials, or historical files and exist only for local recovery.
consequences: Migration ensures the backup pattern is present in the project .gitignore before publication.

decisions.statement: Self-hosted quality gates must reference tools installed by the repository
decisions.reasoning: A migrated command can be syntactically safe yet unavailable in the current project, causing false operational failure.
consequences: The AutoForge repository retains typecheck, formatting, and test gates but removes its unavailable ESLint gate.

decisions.statement: Quality command timeouts must terminate the entire spawned process tree
decisions.reasoning: Killing only an npm parent leaves test runners active, causes resource contention, and makes later checks nondeterministic.
consequences: Use an isolated POSIX process group and group termination, with direct child termination as the portable fallback.

decisions.statement: Foundation tests must use bounded worker concurrency
decisions.reasoning: Running every test file at default parallelism creates filesystem and process contention that causes otherwise passing integration tests to exceed local timeouts.
consequences: Vitest uses at most four workers while preserving per-file isolation and existing timeouts.

decisions.statement: Intent is a durable typed artifact linked to work, specifications, and research.
decisions.reasoning: Intent must preserve raw user input and progressively structured fields without pretending incomplete information is complete.
consequences: Add an intent schema and registry-backed storage; work items reference intent IDs.

decisions.statement: Triage is a deterministic multi-label service.
decisions.reasoning: The same request must produce repeatable classifications before any agent-specific behavior or model call.
consequences: Implement pure triage rules with explicit evidence and golden fixtures.

decisions.statement: Readiness is an explainable heuristic, never a claim of certainty.
decisions.reasoning: Missing requirements must remain visible and confidence scores must not hide unknowns.
consequences: Return known fields, missing evidence, labels, and an optional bounded score.

decisions.statement: Research records are first-class linked artifacts.
decisions.reasoning: Research findings, sources, alternatives, and recommendations need durable provenance and must connect to decisions and specifications.
consequences: Add a research specification type with confidence and source metadata.

decisions.statement: Planning artifacts are modular projections, not a monolithic generated document.
decisions.reasoning: Different requests require different planning outputs and irrelevant context should remain excluded.
consequences: Compile feature briefs, technical plans, design briefs, stories, and acceptance criteria independently.

decisions.statement: 0.8 extends the v0.7 registry and packet contracts additively.
decisions.reasoning: Existing work, state, specification, resolver, adapter, and packet behavior is the released compatibility baseline.
consequences: Preserve current IDs and formats; add migrations only for unavoidable schema changes.

decisions.statement: The 0.8 architecture decision set is approved as the baseline for schema implementation.
decisions.reasoning: The reviewed decisions preserve v0.7 compatibility while defining intent, triage, readiness, research, and modular planning boundaries.
consequences: Proceed to resolve the remaining schema-level decisions, then implement intent and research contracts.

decisions.statement: Intent is stored as a registry-backed specification with raw and structured fields; work stores only the intent reference.
decisions.reasoning: Intent is project knowledge and should use the existing specification identity, relationships, codec, and resolver rather than a parallel state domain.
consequences: Add an intent type and preserve raw input plus optional structured fields in the specification body and metadata.

decisions.statement: One intent may produce multiple work items through explicit intent relationships.
decisions.reasoning: A single request can yield research, design, architecture, and implementation tasks without duplicating the source intent.
consequences: Use typed outgoing work references and preserve independent lifecycle state for each work item.

decisions.statement: Triage labels are additive; conflicts are reported rather than hidden by precedence.
decisions.reasoning: Requests can legitimately require research and design or clarification and architecture at the same time.
consequences: Return all matching labels, evidence, and a conflict flag; do not collapse the result to one winner.

decisions.statement: Readiness requires objective evidence fields and reports missing evidence by work kind.
decisions.reasoning: A universal checklist would overstate readiness for different request classes.
consequences: Define minimum evidence profiles for implementation, research, architecture, and design work.

decisions.statement: Readiness confidence uses a bounded categorical level plus an optional percentage for display.
decisions.reasoning: Categories communicate uncertainty better while a bounded percentage supports progress reporting.
consequences: Every score includes evidence and missing-field explanations; no score is treated as a guarantee.

decisions.statement: Research sources require provenance type, locator, captured timestamp, and confidence when available.
decisions.reasoning: Research must remain auditable across local files, URLs, agent observations, and human notes.
consequences: Represent sources as typed records and permit unavailable locators only with an explicit explanation.

decisions.statement: The canonical v0.8 token type remains token; design-token is a documentation alias only.
decisions.reasoning: The v0.7 registry already ships token IDs and changing the prefix would create unnecessary migration risk.
consequences: Accept token in schemas and map any imported design-token terminology to token without changing identity.

decisions.statement: Generated planning artifacts store source fingerprints and freshness metadata.
decisions.reasoning: Planning outputs must be reproducible and visibly stale when their inputs change.
consequences: Persist generated artifacts with source IDs, revisions or hashes, generator version, and generated timestamp.

decisions.statement: Antigravity and agy are aliases for the canonical gemini agent contract
decisions.reasoning: The Gemini adapter already delivers both Gemini CLI and Antigravity instructions, while maintaining separate capability IDs would create drift. Aliases preserve user-facing terminology without duplicating contracts.
consequences: Normalize antigravity and agy to gemini when generating contracts; keep gemini as the canonical agentId and capability definition.

decisions.statement: Every implementation change must update the relevant documentation before completion
decisions.reasoning: AutoForge is used by multiple agentic AIs and users; undocumented behavior creates drift between the CLI, contracts, workflows, and actual implementation.
consequences: Each task must identify affected documentation, update it within scope, and include documentation validation in its completion evidence.

decisions.statement: Project-scoped single-file stores must resolve null instead of throwing ENOENT before initialization
decisions.reasoning: Constitution, domain, and planning stores crashed with raw uncaught ENOENT stack traces when read before init, unlike the twin store's graceful null-return convention discovered during a north-star roadmap coverage audit. Every command using these stores must handle a null result.
consequences: ConstitutionStore.load(), DomainStore.load(), and PlanningArtifactStore.read()/isFresh() now return null/false on a missing file; new callers must null-check before use.
CLI commands report a friendly EXIT_CODE.invalidState message naming the init command instead of an unhandled exception.

decisions.statement: Issue and task completion requires a linked decision record or an explicit, audited skip reason
decisions.reasoning: CHANGELOG.md silently stopped tracking releases after v0.6.0 because documentation was advisory rather than enforced, and this was only discovered by manual audit across agent handoffs where no human was present to catch the omission.
consequences: autoforge done blocks issue/task completion without a relatedWork-linked decision; autoforge done --no-decision <reason> bypasses it but records the reason as a skip-reason decision.
autoforge changelog compile renders bugfix/feature-note decisions since the last tag into CHANGELOG.md, closing the specific gap that motivated this change.

decisions.statement: Added dedicated data and security work kinds to the shared intent/workflow vocabulary
decisions.reasoning: Bootstrap's gate list requires data and security artifacts but no correctly-labeled intent or workflow kind existed for either; users had to mislabel this work as architecture.
consequences: READINESS_WORK_KINDS and WORKFLOW_KINDS gained data/data-change and security/security-change; both have dedicated workflow definitions with research(optional)->planning->implementation->validation(required) stages.

decisions.statement: Persisted planning artifacts are now namespaced by source fingerprint instead of a flat kind-only path
decisions.reasoning: intent assess --artifact <kind> --persist previously wrote to a fixed .autoforge/planning/<kind>.json path, silently overwriting any prior artifact of the same kind with no warning.
consequences: PlanningArtifactStore stores artifacts at .autoforge/planning/<kind>/<sourceFingerprint>.json; read(kind) with no fingerprint returns the most recent version; a new listVersions(kind) method and updated planning list surface every stored version.

decisions.statement: Newly registered projects now default to an active lifecycle, and the mutation-blocked error names the exact fix command
decisions.reasoning: registerProject left lifecycle undefined, which projectMutationBlocked treats as blocked while projects list/show already displayed it as active -- an undiscoverable, inconsistent trap that silently blocked every mutating use command against a freshly attached project.
consequences: registerProject sets lifecycle: active on first registration (preserving an existing explicit lifecycle on re-registration); the blocked-command stderr message now includes the exact autoforge projects update --lifecycle active fix.

decisions.statement: Generated user-stories artifacts no longer mangle acronyms or repeat the objective clause on every line
decisions.reasoning: The prior template called toLowerCase() on the full requirement string, destroying leading acronyms/proper nouns, and appended a generic so the stated objective is achieved phrase verbatim to every single requirement line, producing barely grammatical boilerplate.
consequences: The user-stories template now lowercases only a non-acronym leading word, strips redundant trailing punctuation before appending a period, and states the shared objective once in a header line instead of once per story. Actor extraction and compound-requirement splitting remain explicitly out of scope as a separate, harder NLP problem.
